search_scope: Primary papers, publisher accepted manuscripts, author-hosted arXiv records and author institutional publication lists; searches for 3D multihyperuniform point patterns, multicomponent spectral/concentration structure factors and finite-size estimation through 2026-10-08. Not an exhaustive systematic review.

sources.citation: S. Torquato, G. Zhang and F. H. Stillinger, Ensemble Theory for Stealthy Hyperuniform Disordered Ground States, Physical Review X 5, 021020 (2015).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed; journal reference and related DOI verified in arXiv record
claims_supported: Stealthy disordered hyperuniform constructions and ensemble theory are studied in dimensions 1, 2 and 3.
Constraint density and sampling of the ground-state manifold matter.
limitations: Single-component framework; does not validate LARP five-component 3D feasibility or learning advantage.
No LARP CPU timing extrapolation supported.
sources.implementation_relevance: Separate constrained mode counts, physical bandwidth and spatial dimension when designing a new 3D finite certificate.

sources.citation: D. Chen, X. Jiang, D. Wang, J. Ilyssa Vidallon, H. L. Zhuang and Y. Jiao, Multihyperuniform long-range order in medium-entropy alloys, Acta Materialia 246, 118678 (2023).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed publication verified on author institutional list; publisher page returned 403; specific method details read from 2021 preprint, not asserted identical to final article
claims_supported: Multihyperuniform assignments of Si, Ge and Sn are constructed on a volumetric diamond lattice.
The accessed manuscript reports five configurations of N=5832, spectral objectives using type swaps, emergent short-range ordering and finite residual low-k power instead of exact stealthiness.
limitations: Lattice-constrained ternary material model, not free five-component continuum geometry.
Material energy/thermal/electronic outcomes cannot be transferred to neural computation.
Preprint author list lacks J. Ilyssa Vidallon, present in published citation; preserve this version distinction.
sources.implementation_relevance: Direct prior art removes novelty of the claim that multihyperuniformity can exist in 3D; simultaneous local-order changes motivate explicit matching.

sources.citation: E. Lomba, J.-J. Weis and S. Torquato, Disordered multihyperuniformity derived from binary plasmas, Physical Review E 97, 010102 (2018).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed; accepted manuscript identifies published journal article and publication date 2018-01-10
claims_supported: Total hyperuniformity need not imply component hyperuniformity in a mixture.
Partial and cross structure factors and concentration-concentration fluctuations distinguish multihyperuniformity from global density suppression.
limitations: Demonstrated model is a two-dimensional binary hard-disk plasma; no direct LARP 3D generation result.
Normalization conventions differ from per-species normalized LARP S_c.
sources.implementation_relevance: Keep total-density and concentration channels separate; record cross spectra alongside diagonal component spectra.

sources.citation: H. Wang, R. Samajdar and S. Torquato, Correlations in interacting electron liquids: Many-body statistics and hyperuniformity, Physical Review B 110, 104201 (2024).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed; arXiv lists Accepted at PRB and Phys. Rev. B 110, 104201 (2024)
claims_supported: Total and spin-resolved spectra are analyzed for quasi-1D, 2D and 3D electron liquids.
Partially polarized liquids can have hyperuniform union and components with different scaling classes.
limitations: Quantum/effective classical physical models do not establish LARP utility or feasibility with its exclusion and species counts.
HTML dynamically displayed a 2026 document date although arXiv submission and journal reference are 2024; use verified publication metadata.
sources.implementation_relevance: A 3D claim must specify whether it concerns total density, every component, concentration contrasts or scaling exponents.

sources.citation: H. Frusawa, Theoretical Basis for Classifying Hyperuniform States of Two-Component Systems, Axioms 14(1), 39 (2025).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed; arXiv journal reference/DOI verified, official publisher search result supports same citation
claims_supported: Theoretical classification distinguishes global, component and cross-correlation behaviors in binary systems.
Suppressed sums and suppressed differences have distinct conditions.
limitations: Binary theoretical classification is not a five-component finite-sample certifier.
Do not apply every thermodynamic stability classification to LARP's non-equilibrium numerical objective.
sources.implementation_relevance: Use the multicomponent covariance matrix and a declared concentration contrast space; the four-dimensional contrast proposal for five species is own algebraic inference.

sources.citation: Y. Jiao, Spectral leakage and masking effects in the measurement of hyperuniformity, Journal of Chemical Physics 164, 224106 (2026).
sources.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed; journal reference and DOI verified in author arXiv record and institutional publication list; DOI fetch unavailable
claims_supported: Finite observation windows and masks convolve intrinsic spectra and can distort apparent small-k scaling.
Scaling exponents require an appropriate range of accessible scales.
limitations: A cropped/masked observation differs from a complete periodic simulation sampled at reciprocal-lattice modes; do not claim the same leakage is necessarily present in current LARP.
Abstract consulted; no replication or quantitative validation performed.
sources.implementation_relevance: Declare boundary and estimator conventions; treat a small finite certificate separately from asymptotic hyperuniformity.

sources.citation: Y. Liu, X. Li, J. Tian, X. Yan and G. Zhang, Extracting effective scaling exponents in finite-size hyperuniform systems, arXiv:2606.18848v1 (2026).
sources.peer_review_status: preprint; accessed arXiv record has no journal reference or acceptance statement
claims_supported: Finite-sample effective exponent estimation depends on accessible scales and method-specific fitting windows.
The manuscript proposes a protocol combining structure-factor, number-variance and spreadability estimates.
limitations: Proposal not independently validated here; does not justify LARP certificate thresholds or an N400 asymptotic exponent.
Correlated diagnostics must not be counted as independent evidence.
sources.implementation_relevance: Context for finite-size diagnostics only; not a required implementation or authority to run experiments.

own_inferences: For unit numerical density, N400 implies L2D=20 and L3D=400^(1/3), and reciprocal k_min=2*pi/L; dimensional densities require a declared reference length.

Integer wavevectors with 0<|n|<=2 contain six conjugate pairs in 2D and sixteen in 3D; sixteen complex species amplitudes impose at most 32 real equations, compared with 3*(34-1)=99 relative coordinate degrees for E34 before other constraints.

Five concentration amplitudes eta_c=rho_c-f_c*rho_union sum to zero, so their covariance has at most four independent contrast directions; a single mode outer product has rank one and needs averaging before spectral eigenvalue interpretation.
Holding N, numerical density, native kNN graph, full distance distribution, hop profiles and wiring cost simultaneously is generally incompatible with a genuine spatial-dimension intervention.
The proposed 3D preflight, gates, resource ceilings and sequencing are research recommendations, not executed or externally validated results.
